This bundles two assumptions the matrix does not isolate: (1) a TOPOLOGY assumption that the institution can physically hold its own HSM/Vault and trust anchor on premises (related to but distinct from ANCHOR-SELF-HOST-CUSTODY: this row is the key/anchor custody location specifically and its role as the scoring optimum); and (2) a JURISDICTION assumption that on-premises custody is both achievable and the strongest posture -- the 'no third-country disclosure regime' criterion presupposes the EU 'third-country' framing AND a local legal order under which on-prem custody actually defeats disclosure (a domestic compelled-access regime can reach an on-premises HSM, so 'on-prem = Robust' is jurisdiction-relative). Generalise so the data-dimension optimum is 'custody arrangement that minimises the applicable disclosure-regime exposure' rather than hard-coding on-premises custody, and gate the 'no third-country disclosure regime' criterion behind the adopter's jurisdiction profile.
